title: 2. The Hook: How to Grab Readers from Chapter One
use_cases: Use when drafting the opening pages of a fictional manuscript
Implement when revising a story to improve reader retention
Configure when balancing exposition and action in early chapters
Use when establishing the protagonist's primary motivation quickly
content:
If you don’t hook your readers in the first few paragraphs, they won’t stick around. So, do the following:

- Start with conflict, intrigue, or an emotional moment.
- Introduce the main character’s goal or problem quickly.
- Avoid info dumps — weave world-building naturally into the story.

The faster you get into the heart of the story, the more likely readers will stay invested. If you want to read more on how you can hook your readers from Chapter One, I have a published article on it so you can click on this link https://tinyurl.com/Hook-your-readers to help you out with it.
